astra_actions.research_notes: Changing direction from further HGB memorization: confirmation:2 and confirmation:3 show that near-zero paid fit did not generalize. analysis:332 produced only a printing error, not a new model result. The pulse and constant-control evidence suggests a three-step sum (analysis:30, analysis:38, analysis:46), with an x-linear and z-quadratic upper-c branch (analysis:52). Crucially, changing only current c switches the whole steady response immediately (analysis:88), suggesting current c selects the readout of the entire recent window rather than each historical c selecting its own contribution. analysis:85 brackets the switch between -0.17625 and -0.176. This run tests that previously neglected composition on all paid data, fitting only rows before 3357 and reporting the last two complete records separately as a retrospective holdout. If shared polynomial sums fail, separate lag weights are the immediate alternative; no new confirmation is justified yet.

analysis:333 identifies a compact law: current c selects one of two readouts of [window count, sum(x), sum(z^2)] over the current and two preceding controls. Fitting before row 3357 gave retrospective held-out MSE 1.34e-29 on records 173–174; all-row maximum error was 1.42e-14. Historical c and longer memory are unnecessary for these observations. This replaces the unsuccessful HGB approach (confirmation:2, confirmation:3). Installing the reduced six-coefficient predictor and evaluating it will detect transcription or term-removal errors; any mismatch would require repairing the implementation before submission. Limitation: -0.176125 is a working switch value consistent with paid data, not an exactly identified threshold (analysis:85, analysis:333). After successful evaluation, narrow that remaining switch interval with a small targeted acquisition, then request fresh confirmation.

analysis:333 supports current-c gating of a three-control window with branch-specific coefficients on count, sum(x), and sum(z²). The installed shared/gated_window.py now passes all 3453 paid rows with MSE 5.35e-30 (current_paid_evaluation); implementation verification is complete. Representation collisions have only floating-point-scale label differences, with empirical MSE floor 3.05e-34, not a meaningful missing-input error. Unlike this compact model, HGB failed confirmation:2 and confirmation:3. Remaining uncertainty is the switch location: analysis:85 and analysis:102 bracket it between -0.1762 and -0.176. This 15-row sweep detects misclassification by the working threshold -0.176125; use the observed transition to narrow and revise that threshold before fresh confirmation. Unexpected non-branch outputs would instead challenge the gating law.

analysis:333 and the paid evaluation support a current-c-gated three-control sum with six coefficients. record:175 now contradicts the installed threshold -0.176125: c=-0.17615 already yields the upper-c branch. Read the complete sweep, including omitted row 3455, to identify the new bracket. This analysis distinguishes a threshold-only error from failure of either branch formula; update the executable threshold if all outputs match a branch, then evaluate and request fresh confirmation. Earlier HGB failures (confirmation:2, confirmation:3) do not test this compact law.

analysis:336 resolves the previously unread sweep: record:175 brackets the switch between -0.1761625 and -0.17615, and every paid output matches one established branch within 8.22e-15. Update only the threshold to the bracket midpoint. analysis:333 supports the shared three-control sum; the representation collision floor (~3e-34) is numerical roundoff, not a material omitted-state effect. This evaluation checks whether the installed threshold repair reproduces all 3468 rows; material residuals would require inspecting their branch assignments before submission. If it passes, request fresh confirmation of this compact law, which confirmation:2 and confirmation:3 did not test. Exact switch location within the bracket remains unresolved.

analysis:333 supports the compact gated three-control sum; analysis:336 and record:175 locate the switch bracket. Request fresh confirmation to detect failure on independent trajectories; if it fails, inspect whether counterexamples indicate threshold misclassification or a branch-law error. confirmation:2 and confirmation:3 tested HGB predictors, not this law.
